The trash attributes deletions to the wrong person. There is no record of who
deleted a document, so the trash infers the deleting user from
`lastModifiedById`. That has two bad effects:

- When someone deletes a page that has nested pages, every nested page shows
  whoever last edited it, not the person who deleted the tree.
- Deleting a document rewrites the edit history: the deleter becomes the
  `lastModifiedById` of the document and all of its descendants.

Please record the deleting user properly, on the server side:

- Documents get a `deletedById` column (a nullable reference to a user).
- Soft-deleting a document records the acting user in `deletedById`. This
  includes nested documents deleted along with their parent. Restoring a
  document clears it.
- Deleting no longer changes `lastModifiedById` on any of the documents.
- Document API responses (for example `documents.info` and `documents.deleted`)
  include `deletedBy`, the presented user who deleted the document, for deleted
  documents. Documents that are not deleted have no `deletedBy`.
- The existing `deletedById` filter on `documents.deleted` keeps working.

The web client is out of scope.

**What changed**
- **Migration** (`server/migrations/20261019120000-add-deletedById-to-documents.js`): adds a nullable `deletedById` column referencing `users`. It also fills it in for documents already in the trash, using their current `lastModifiedById`, so existing trash entries keep their attribution and the filter still finds them. I applied it, rolled it back and re-applied it on the test database.
- **Deleting a document** (`Document.destroyWithCtx`, `Collection.deleteDocument`): records the acting user on the document and every nested document, and no longer rewrites `lastModifiedById` on any of them. Deleting a whole collection also records the deleter on its documents now; before, it overwrote `lastModifiedById`.
- **Restoring** (`Document.restoreTo`): clears `deletedById`.
- **API responses** (`server/presenters/document.ts`): deleted documents include `deletedBy` as a presented user; other documents don't have the field. `documents.deleted` loads the user in the same query. Other endpoints, such as `documents.info`, look the user up separately, and only for deleted documents.
- **Filter on `documents.deleted`**: `deletedById` now filters on the real column instead of being mapped to `lastModifiedById`.

**One thing to review:** the save after deletion is what publishes the `documents.delete` event. The old code triggered it by changing `lastModifiedById`. Now that `deletedById` is already written during the soft delete, that save could find nothing changed and skip the event. So I explicitly mark `deletedById` as changed to keep the event firing. A test checks that the event is emitted with the deleting user as the actor.

**Tests**
- I updated the existing tests that expected the deleter in `lastModifiedById`.
- New tests cover:
  - deleting a three-level tree, where every level gets the deleter while `lastModifiedById` stays the same;
  - restoring, which clears the field;
  - `documents.info` returning `deletedBy` for deleted documents and leaving it out otherwise;
  - the `deletedById` filter on nested documents;
  - collection deletion.
